item.title: DLE 2026-05-17
item.description:
1. The Funny One

"Tech Twitter is just people who made money telling people who haven't made money that they're thinking about making money wrong."

2. Business Insight

A — Greene (Mastery): The Three Phases. Apprenticeship → Creative-Active → Mastery. No shortcuts. Stay in the work.

B — Carnegie: Begin in a Friendly Way. Sun beats wind. Open hard conversations with warmth and shared ground.

3. Deep Line

"A myth cannot be refuted, since it is identical with the convictions of a group." — Sorel. The Kiln's positioning isn't a claim to prove — it's a myth to embody.

4. Thought Principle: Working Backwards (Bezos). Start with customer need, not your current skills.

5. New Words: Hyperbolic Discounting (over-valuing immediate vs future rewards), Asymmetric Information (the gap you monetize), Pareto Optimality (the equilibrium where any change makes someone worse off)

6. Stoic: "The wound is the place where the Light enters you." — Rumi

7. Daily Math: Regression to the Mean. Extreme results regress toward the average. Most "breakthroughs" and "crises" are just outliers. Judge on long-run averages.

Next: Pareto Distribution.

item.title: DLE 2026-05-15
item.description:
1. The Funny One

"A seed round is just paying for the privilege of finding out your idea doesn't work. A Series A is paying to find out it works but not the way you thought."

2. Business Insight

A — Cialdini: Social Proof Under Uncertainty. ICP-matched case studies beat generic ones. Stack proof where doubt is highest.

B — Bezos: Input Metrics Over Output Metrics. Track enriched leads, response rates, meetings booked. If inputs are world-class, revenue follows.

3. Deep Line

"The optimist in politics is an inconstant and even dangerous man." — Sorel. The "we're a family" founder fires coldest.

4. Thought Principle: Definite vs Indefinite Optimism (Thiel). Have a concrete plan, not vague iteration.

5. New Words: Goodhart's Law (when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be good), Counterfactual Thinking (what would have happened without you?), Shibboleth (language that signals group membership)

6. Stoic: "Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect." — Marcus Aurelius

7. Daily Math: Confidence Intervals. The width of your CI is your ignorance. 10 data points = wide interval = you know almost nothing. 100 = tight = trustworthy.

Next: Regression to the Mean.

item.title: DLE 2026-05-14
item.description:
1. The Funny One

"Every startup deck says 'if we capture just 1% of the market...' and every VC knows that 1% is the hardest 1% you'll ever capture."

2. Business Insight

A — Carnegie: Let the client feel the idea is theirs. Plant ideas through questions, not presentations. They'll champion "their" idea with 10x the energy.

B — Greene (Mastery): Skill-Stacking. Your moat is the combination of skills, not any single one. Keep adding layers.

3. Deep Line

"Only power restrains power." — Burnham

4. Thought Principle: The Contrast Principle (Cialdini). Always show the big scary number before your price.

5. New Words: Skin in the Game (personal downside exposure), Chesterton's Fence (understand before removing), Satisficing (good enough beats optimal)

6. Stoic: "It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare, it is because we do not dare that they are difficult." — Seneca

7. Daily Math: Normal Distribution. 68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2, 99.7% within 3. Most "crises" are just normal variance.

Next: Confidence Intervals.

item.title: DLE 2026-05-13
item.description:
1. The Funny One

"The best investment advice I ever got was 'invest in things you understand.' The worst advice I ever got was also that, because I understood nothing."

2. Business Insight

A — Cialdini: Authority Through Vulnerability (Vincent Strategy). Argue against your own interest once. It buys total credibility for the upsell.

B — Collins: Stop-Doing Lists > To-Do Lists. The discipline is in subtracting. Cut one thing this week.

3. Deep Line

"From mean to great fortune, people rise rather by fraud than by force." — Machiavelli

4. Thought Principle: The Commitment Blueprint (Grant). Hire for values + make dissent a core value. Zero percent failure rate in the study.

5. New Words: Iatrogenic (harm by the healer), Second-Order Thinking (and then what?), Legibility (forcing messy reality into neat systems)

6. Stoic: "We suffer more often in imagination than in reality." — Seneca

7. Daily Math: Standard Deviation & Variance. Same average, different spread = different reality. Always ask "what's the spread?" when someone gives you an average.

Next: Normal Distribution.

item.title: DLE 2026-05-12
item.description:
1. The Funny One

"I'm 27, I run a company, and I still call my mam when the washing machine makes a weird noise. That's the duality of entrepreneurship."

2. Business Insight

A — Bezos: Customer Obsession. Clients aren't loyal — they're satisfied until someone offers something better.

B — 48 Laws, Law 11: Make Yourself Indispensable. Embed in the client's workflow. Own their Clay tables, enrichment, sequences. Make switching cost enormous through depth, not lock-in.

3. Deep Line

"The representative has himself elected by the voters, not the voters who choose the representative." — Mosca

4. Thought Principle: First Who, Then What (Collins)

Get the right people on the bus before figuring out where to drive it.

5. New Words: Iatrogenic (harm by the healer), Kaizen (continuous improvement), Apophenia (seeing patterns that don't exist)

6. Stoic: "The soul becomes dyed with the colour of its thoughts." — Marcus Aurelius

7. Daily Math: Law of Large Numbers. Under 30 data points? Treat any pattern as noise. Increase sample size before optimizing.

Next: Standard Deviation & Variance.

item.title: DLE 2026-05-11
item.description:
1. The Funny One

"People ask me what The Kiln does and I say 'we help companies find people who want to talk to them' and they say 'so... marketing?' and I die a little inside."

2. Business Insight

A — Thiel: Distribution IS the Product. Most startups die from distribution failure, not product failure. The Kiln solves the most common cause of startup death.

B — Cialdini: Foot-in-the-Door. Small commitments change self-image. Free audits and quick wins aren't charity — they're commitment devices. 76% vs 17% compliance.

3. Deep Line

"It is easier to cope with a bad conscience than with a bad reputation." — Nietzsche

4. Thought Principle: The Sarick Effect (Grant)

Lead with your biggest flaws when pitching skeptical audiences. It disarms skepticism and increases persuasion. Rufus Griscom sold Babble to Disney for $40M after a slide titled "Here's Why You Should Not Buy Babble."

5. New Words & Terms

Convexity — Limited downside, uncapped upside. Only take convex bets.

Overton Window — The range of acceptable ideas in public discourse. Position yourself where the window is moving.

Praxis — The integration of theory and practice. Not just knowing, but doing informed by knowing.

6. Stoic Closer

"First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do." — Epictetus

7. Daily Math: Bayes' Theorem

P(A|B) = P(B|A) × P(A) / P(B). Update beliefs when new evidence arrives. Anchor on the base rate first, then adjust. Your gut skips base rates — Bayes doesn't.

Next: Law of Large Numbers.
